residual_findings.title: POST /memory/review has_more false-completion when final/only row times out or fails and remains pending (process_review_batch counts timed-out/failed attempts as processed)
residual_findings.note: Blocks full closure of R-V178P0-QC3-003 client-completion axis. Fix: track queue advancement separately from rows attempted; on row-level timeout/failure that leaves the row pending, ensure has_more=true. Add regression tests for one-row timeout, final-row timeout, perpetually-failing head row.
residual_findings.closure_note: Fixed in commit e7417c99 (fix/v1.80-review-has-more-completion, merged as 530070c3). process_review_batch now tracks any_row_remained_pending flag (set in both Ok(0,0,0) action-failure + Err(_elapsed) timeout arms); review derives has_more = more_in_db || deadline_stopped || any_row_remained_pending. 3 regression tests added (single-row fail, final-row fail, perpetually-failing row) — verified FAIL pre-fix. qc3 targeted re-review (7e9dacf3) flipped to Approve; all 3 R-V178P0-QC3-003 axes now Addressed.

residual_findings.title: memory_review_locks HashMap unbounded per-creator (entries never evicted; daemon-lifetime)
residual_findings.target: V1.80+ (document lifecycle ceiling; revisit if multi-creator/session churn becomes real)
residual_findings.note: Local single-active-creator daemon: ~1 entry at a time. Acceptable for current threat model. Add a lifecycle comment noting the simplification; replace with eviction/DB-lock if multi-creator churn materializes.
residual_findings.closure_note: Documented in V1.81 P-last: memory_review_locks lifecycle ceiling (workspace/mod.rs) + delete_pending_by_id at-least-once threat model (memory.rs).

residual_findings.title: best-effort delete_pending_by_id after side-effect success leaves re-processing window (at-least-once under threat model)
residual_findings.target: V1.80+ (pre-existing V1.33 best-effort pattern; at-least-once accepted under local-only/single-creator/small-queue threat model)
residual_findings.note: If delete fails after a successful promote/fragment, the pending row remains and the next review re-processes it (duplicate promote/fragment). Per-creator mutex prevents within-cycle double-processing; cross-cycle re-processing is the at-least-once trade-off. Accepted under documented threat model; raise severity if queue size or writer count increases.
residual_findings.closure_note: Documented in V1.81 P-last: memory_review_locks lifecycle ceiling (workspace/mod.rs) + delete_pending_by_id at-least-once threat model (memory.rs).
